Vegetative.visual_clues: Green lush foliage with upright leafy tillers; no swollen boot or emerged flower panicles visible in canopy.
Vegetative.irrigation: Maintain a shallow water layer of 2 - 3 cm in the field. Avoid deep submergence or drying during active tillering.
Vegetative.fertilizer: Apply the recommended top-dressing dose of Nitrogen (Urea) in 2 splits. Ensure Zinc Sulfate is applied if deficiency chlorosis appears.
Vegetative.pest_disease_watch: Watch for Rice Leaf Folder, Green Leafhopper, and early Bacterial Leaf Blight or Blast.
Vegetative.priority_action: Promote tiller development with shallow water and scheduled split application of Urea.

Reproductive.visual_clues: Swollen flag leaf sheath (booting) or fully emerged panicles with delicate white flowering florets shedding pollen.
Reproductive.irrigation: Critical water stage: maintain 5 cm standing water continuously. Moisture stress now will cause sterile empty spikelets (chaffy grain).
Reproductive.fertilizer: Apply Muriate of Potash (MOP) at panicle initiation to boost grain filling. Avoid high Nitrogen which invites fungal diseases.
Reproductive.pest_disease_watch: High susceptibility to Neck Blast, Sheath Blight, Stem Borer, and Brown Planthopper (BPH).
Reproductive.priority_action: Ensure uninterrupted irrigation and scout daily for Neck Blast and Brown Planthopper.

Ripening.visual_clues: Panicles bend gracefully under grain weight; foliage turns from green to golden yellow; grains harden and dry.
Ripening.irrigation: Keep soil moist during dough stage, then drain all standing water 10 - 14 days prior to expected harvest.
Ripening.fertilizer: No soil fertilizer needed. Optional foliar 1% Potassium Nitrate if late grain filling needs support.
Ripening.pest_disease_watch: Watch for False Smut, Earhead Bug (Gundhi bug), and bird damage.
Ripening.priority_action: Drain field water 10 days before harvest to facilitate uniform grain drying and easy combine/manual harvesting.

Vegetative.visual_clues: Stout green stalks with broad arching leaves; no visible tassels at crown or silk emergence on ear shoots.
Vegetative.irrigation: Irrigate at knee-high stage (V6-V8). Maize cannot tolerate waterlogging; ensure ridge-and-furrow drainage.
Vegetative.fertilizer: Side-dress Nitrogen (Urea) at knee-high stage (30-35 DAS). Apply Zinc if white bud deficiency appears.
Vegetative.pest_disease_watch: Scout aggressively for Fall Armyworm (FAW) inside leaf whorls and Common Rust.
Vegetative.priority_action: Side-dress Urea and apply targeted biological or registered control for Fall Armyworm in the central whorl.

Reproductive.visual_clues: Crown tassels actively shedding pollen; ears develop moist cream-to-pink silks ready for fertilization.
Reproductive.irrigation: Most moisture-critical phase in maize life. Water deficit during silking causes severe pollination failure and barren cobs.
Reproductive.fertilizer: Apply final split of Potash and light Nitrogen if soil fertility is low. Avoid foliar burn during hot hours.
Reproductive.pest_disease_watch: Corn Earworm, Turcicum Leaf Blight, and Southern Rust.
Reproductive.priority_action: Maintain soil moisture at 70-80% field capacity to ensure complete silk pollination and full kernel set.

Ripening.visual_clues: Husk leaves turn dry and straw-colored; silks brown and brittle; kernels dent and develop a black physiological abscission layer.
Ripening.irrigation: Taper off irrigation. Stop watering completely 10-14 days before harvest.
Ripening.pest_disease_watch: Stalk Rots and kernel rots if unseasonable rains occur.
Ripening.priority_action: Monitor kernel moisture; harvest when husks are paper-dry and grain moisture drops below 20%.

Vegetative.visual_clues: Dark green lobed leaves forming a pyramidal bush; small triangular flower buds (squares) starting to emerge.
Vegetative.irrigation: Light, controlled irrigation. Excessive moisture at this stage causes excessive vegetative rank growth rather than fruiting.
Vegetative.fertilizer: Apply first top-dressing of Nitrogen + Potash at 35-45 DAS. Foliar Magnesium Sulfate if interveinal reddening appears.
Vegetative.pest_disease_watch: Sucking pests: Whitefly, Jassids, Thrips, and Aphids; Bacterial Blight.
Vegetative.priority_action: Control sucking pests early to protect young squares from shedding and avoid excessive vegetative growth.

local_names.hi: फूल एवं गूलर (Boll) बनने की अवस्था (Reproductive)

Reproductive.visual_clues: Canopy shows creamy white and reddish-pink flowers alongside expanding green round bolls.
Reproductive.irrigation: Peak water requirement. Irrigate every 8-12 days depending on soil texture. Water stress causes heavy square and young boll drop.
Reproductive.fertilizer: Foliar spray of 1% Potassium Nitrate (KNO3) or 2% DAP every 15 days to nourish developing bolls and prevent dropping.
Reproductive.pest_disease_watch: Bollworms (Spotted, American, and Pink Bollworm), Alternaria Leaf Spot, and Grey Mildew.
Reproductive.priority_action: Spray 1% Potassium Nitrate to reduce boll shedding and deploy pheromone traps for Pink Bollworm monitoring.

Ripening.visual_clues: Lower and middle green bolls split wide open into 4-5 carpels revealing clean, dry, fluffy white lint.
Ripening.irrigation: Cease irrigation completely to avoid staining lint and allow uniform boll bursting.
Ripening.pest_disease_watch: Staining fungi if untimely rain hits; Pink Bollworm inside unburst bolls.
Ripening.priority_action: Pick clean white cotton on dry, sunny mornings without leaf trash or bract debris.

local_names.hi: अंकुरण एवं कल्ले फूटने की अवस्था (Tillering)

Vegetative.visual_clues: Young leafy shoots forming clumps of tillers; short green stems with thin early internodes; canopy closing.
Vegetative.irrigation: Irrigate at 7-10 day intervals. Critical for establishing high tiller count per clump.
Vegetative.fertilizer: Apply Nitrogen and Potash in partial splits at 30, 60, and 90 days. Perform partial earthing-up to anchor tillers.
Vegetative.pest_disease_watch: Early Shoot Borer (causes dead hearts), Termites, and Red Rot.
Vegetative.priority_action: Carry out weeding, split Nitrogen application, and earthing up to protect against Early Shoot Borer.

Reproductive.visual_clues: Dense tall jungle-like canopy over 2-3 meters high; thick solid canes with visible nodes and internodes.
Reproductive.irrigation: Water requirement is maximum. Irrigate every 6-8 days. Trash mulching in furrows preserves moisture.
Reproductive.fertilizer: Final application of Nitrogen and full remaining Potash (critical for sucrose synthesis). Detrash lower dry leaves.
Reproductive.pest_disease_watch: Internode Borer, Top Shoot Borer, Rust, and Yellow Leaf Disease.
Reproductive.priority_action: Trash-mulch furrows to conserve water, tie adjacent canes together (propping) to avoid lodging during monsoon winds.

Ripening.visual_clues: Lower foliage dries and sheds naturally; stalk rind turns yellowish, waxy, and brittle; hand refractometer brix exceeds 18-20%.
Ripening.irrigation: Stop irrigation 20 to 25 days before harvest to stress the cane and concentrate sucrose juice in stalks.
Ripening.fertilizer: Strictly do not apply Nitrogen as it causes sugar inversion and low sucrose recovery.
Ripening.pest_disease_watch: Rats, wild boars, and Red Rot in mature stalks.
Ripening.priority_action: Withhold irrigation 3 weeks prior to cutting and cut canes flush with the ground for maximum sugar yield.

Vegetative.visual_clues: Low-growing bushy green foliage with four-parted leaflets; no yellow flowers or underground pegs yet.
Vegetative.irrigation: Light irrigation after sowing and weeding. Avoid excessive soil wetness to prevent collar rot.
Vegetative.fertilizer: Ensure basal application of single superphosphate (SSP) and Rhizobium biofertilizer. Nitrogen should be moderate.
Vegetative.pest_disease_watch: Collar Rot, Root Rot, Thrips, and Aphids.
Vegetative.priority_action: Complete hoeing and weeding before flowering; do not disturb soil after pegs start entering ground.

local_names.hi: फूल एवं सुइयां (Pegs) बनने की अवस्था (Pegging)

Reproductive.visual_clues: Small golden-yellow flowers open at base of leaf axils; needle-like pegs (gynophores) elongate downward and plunge into topsoil.
Reproductive.irrigation: Critical: Keep topsoil moist and soft so pegs can easily penetrate. Hard crusty soil prevents peg entry and causes severe yield loss.
Reproductive.fertilizer: Apply Gypsum @ 400 kg/ha at 40-45 DAS around plant base. Calcium in gypsum is mandatory for shell hardening and pod filling.
Reproductive.pest_disease_watch: Tikka Leaf Spot (Early & Late Leaf Spot), Groundnut Rust, and Tobacco Caterpillar.
Reproductive.priority_action: Apply Gypsum into soil immediately at flowering and maintain soft topsoil moisture for smooth peg penetration.

Ripening.visual_clues: Foliage turns yellowish and starts shedding lower leaves; pulled test pods show prominent reticulate shell veins and dark brown inner pod lining.
Ripening.irrigation: Give one light pre-harvest irrigation 2-3 days before pulling if soil is hard, ensuring pods do not snap off underground.
Ripening.pest_disease_watch: Termites and white grubs attacking subterranean pods.
Ripening.priority_action: Pull sample plants; harvest when 75-80% of test pods show dark brownish inner shell lining.

Vegetative.visual_clues: Upright maize-like stalks with thick waxy leaves showing a prominent central white midrib; no seed head emerged.
Vegetative.irrigation: Drought tolerant, but responds well to irrigation at 30-35 DAS. Drain excess standing rain water.
Vegetative.fertilizer: Side-dress Nitrogen (Urea) at 30-35 DAS. Avoid over-application on dry soils.
Vegetative.pest_disease_watch: Sorghum Shoot Fly (causes dead hearts in first 4 weeks) and Stem Borer.
Vegetative.priority_action: Manage Shoot Fly early and side-dress Urea around the 30-day mark before flag leaf emergence.

local_names.hi: बाली निकलने एवं फूलने की अवस्था (Reproductive)

Reproductive.visual_clues: Dense head/panicle bursts open from top sheath; tiny yellow anthers shed pollen across the panicle florets.
Reproductive.irrigation: Most sensitive water stage. Drought now leads to poor panicle emergence and blank florets.
Reproductive.fertilizer: Ensure adequate soil Potassium. Foliar micro-nutrient spray if deficiency is evident.
Reproductive.pest_disease_watch: Sorghum Midge (damages developing ovaries), Head Bug, Anthracnose, and Rust.
Reproductive.priority_action: Scout during morning hours for Sorghum Midge and protect emerged panicles from sucking head bugs.

Ripening.visual_clues: Panicles turn cream, red, or golden-brown; individual grains become rock hard; small black layer forms at grain attachment point.
Ripening.pest_disease_watch: Grain Molds (if late rains fall on mature panicles) and bird damage.
Ripening.priority_action: Protect panicles from birds and harvest promptly when grains reach hard dough stage to prevent grain mold.

Vegetative.visual_clues: Slender woody stems sprouting palmate, star-like leaves with green or reddish petioles; canopy spreading.
Vegetative.irrigation: Irrigate immediately after planting setts and maintain moderate moisture for initial root development.
Vegetative.fertilizer: Apply basal NPK along with Farmyard Manure. Top-dress first split of Nitrogen and Potash at 60 DAP.
Vegetative.pest_disease_watch: Cassava Mosaic Disease (spread by Whiteflies) and Red Spider Mites.
Vegetative.priority_action: Rogue out any virus-infected mosaic shoots immediately and spray for whitefly vector control.

Reproductive.visual_clues: Dense tall bushy canopy (1.5-2m); ground around base shows soil cracking as subterranean tubers expand.
Reproductive.irrigation: Provide regular irrigation at 10-15 day intervals. Flooding or waterlogging causes severe tuber rot.
Reproductive.fertilizer: Potash is paramount! Apply second heavy dose of Muriate of Potash (MOP) at 90-100 DAP to maximize starch conversion.
Reproductive.pest_disease_watch: Root Rot (Phytophthora / Fusarium in wet soils) and Spiralling Whitefly.
Reproductive.priority_action: Apply high Potash fertilizer and earth-up soil around plant base to prevent tubers from sun-greening.

Ripening.visual_clues: Lower and middle leaves naturally yellow and drop off; stems look bare with a small top tuft; tuber skin peels easily revealing white starch flesh.
Ripening.irrigation: Withhold irrigation 10-15 days prior to harvest so tubers remain firm and starch content is maximum.
Ripening.priority_action: Stop irrigation 2 weeks before harvest to prevent watery tubers and achieve peak starch market value.

Vegetative.visual_clues: Vigorous crown of dark green radiating fronds with no flower spathes or bearing nuts on trunk axils.
Vegetative.irrigation: Irrigate young palms regularly (25-40 liters every 2-3 days). Mulch around ring basin with coconut husk.
Vegetative.fertilizer: Apply NPK fertilizer in circular basin 1.5 meters away from trunk. Add Borax (50g) and Magnesium Sulfate (500g).
Vegetative.pest_disease_watch: Rhinoceros Beetle (V-shaped leaf cuts), Red Palm Weevil, and Bud Rot.
Vegetative.priority_action: Check top spear leaf regularly for Rhinoceros beetle attacks and maintain husk mulch in circular basin.

local_names.hi: पुष्पन एवं बटन (फूल) बनने की अवस्था (Reproductive)

Reproductive.visual_clues: Creamy-yellow branched spadix emerges from leaf axils shedding pollen; tiny marble-sized green buttons (female flowers) set on spikes.
Reproductive.irrigation: Crucial: Bearing palms need 40 - 50 liters water daily through drip/basin. Moisture stress causes massive button dropping.
Reproductive.fertilizer: Apply standard annual dose of 1.3 kg Urea, 2 kg SSP, and 2 kg MOP split into pre-monsoon and post-monsoon doses.
Reproductive.pest_disease_watch: Eriophyid Mite (triangular yellow-brown markings on buttons), Button Shedding, and Tanjore Wilt.
Reproductive.priority_action: Spray 2% Urea + DAP or planofix to minimize premature button drop; ensure daily drip irrigation.

Ripening.visual_clues: Lower frond bunches carry large heavy nuts; husk turns from green to yellowish-brown; tapping gives a metallic ringing sound indicating solid copra.
Ripening.pest_disease_watch: Rats and squirrel damage to mature bunches.
Ripening.priority_action: Harvest mature bunches on a 35-45 day cycle when the outer husk turns brownish-green.
